recipe.observation: Passive read-only polling of the supervisor-exposed JSON event stream only. Parse newline-delimited envelopes by the top-level 'type' discriminator (system/assistant/result). Fingerprint the runtime by the argv flag signature (--bare/--print/--verbose/--output-format/--permission-mode/--no-session-persistence) combined with the event envelope schema. Never attach to the process, never inject input, never write to the workspace or config directories. Re-observe on a live re-run to capture the full cycle and detect tool_call-bearing assistant/result records.
recipe.hook: Event-sink hook on the supervisor-exposed stream: consume assistant and result records to map message_role/content-block and tool-result structure. No active hook into process memory, no file watchers, no plugin/path hooking. If the process is re-observed while alive, hook = subscribe to stream and record cycle boundaries; do not touch the process tree.
recipe.redaction: Redact all envelope field values not on the allowlist (type, message_role, content_block_types, has_text, has_tool_call, subtype). Redact stream key names where marked [REDACTED] by the supervisor. Redact all network peer identifiers (IP/port). Never request, log, or persist credentials, tokens, cookies, API keys, session identifiers, or private key material. Treat any config-like content as secret-bearing until proven otherwise.
recipe.confidence: high: agent-like runtime confirmed by argv shape + single system/assistant/result event cycle + established TCP + clean exit. medium: config file location not directly observable (no config path in argv, no config-like open paths, only .mui resource); configuration appears flag/env driven and read early at startup, with default session store disabled by --no-session-persistence.
recipe.fallback: If the target remains unavailable: classify from the retained supervisor stream snapshot only (counts + type distribution), do not force re-observation. If probe_help/observe become available for a live PID: re-run probe_help, re-scan open paths for config-like extensions, and re-check argv for a config-file flag before committing a config-location fingerprint. If the stream schema changes (new types or fields): fall back to opaque line capture recording only type distribution, and lower confidence on protocol details.
